speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Transport with regard to requests for road safety features, such as speed bumps, zebra crossings, traffic lights and overhead bridges, received from Members of Parliament, residents and members of the public (a) how does the Ministry evaluate such requests; (b) whether the Ministry will re-evaluate the requests upon further studies conducted or following accidents; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider revising its criteria for road safety features around schools and residential areas arising from these requests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The safety of pedestrians is a key consideration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Measures that are assessed to be helpful and practical will be designed and implemented to cater to localised needs, taking into consideration the impact on traffic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These could include traffic calming measures and additional crossings for pedestrians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We have implemented School Zones in the vicinity of every school.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Both zones come with additional road safety features, such as lower speed limits, traffic calming measures and road signs.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I note that LTA would conduct studies and ground assessments when an accident occurs to ascertain that more engineering measures or enforcement actions are needed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, would the Ministry of Transport (MOT) be able to share whether it would work with the Traffic Police and commit more resources to implement traffic calming infrastructure at all major accident hotspots to reduce the risk of another accident?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to thank the Member for the supplementary question.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some of the road infrastructure improvements or road safety enhancement measures that we have been doing and will be doing some more, would be signalised pedestrian crossings, for instance, traffic calming measures which the Member has mentioned, like speed humps, three-dimensional road markings, road signages, narrow and meandering roads as well as, of course, as I have mentioned, School Zones and Silver Zones, that we will continue to implement where there is a high seniors profile, for instance, as well as the newly announced Friendly Street initiative, which we will bring to more residents as well as to all towns by 2030.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And as I have said, we will be doing more.
